candidate_founder_decisions.decision: One shared shell contract across web, iOS, and Android with platform-appropriate presentation but common authority and state semantics.
Desktop/tablet use a persistent or collapsible rail; compact mobile uses a bounded bottom navigation plus an accessible More destination.
Landing and ordering are persona-aware: horse-first for owners, task-first for staff, schedule/training-first for trainers, operations-first for facility administrators.
Multi-tenant and multi-facility users receive an explicit active-context indicator and controlled switcher; context is never silently inferred.
Global search is active-context and permission bound; identifiable cross-tenant discovery is prohibited by default.
A command palette may navigate and invoke bounded actions, with separate execution-time authorization.
Quick Create is limited to registered domain-owned forms and current create authority.
Recents, pins, favorites, and saved views are private, reauthorized on every read, and suppressed when authority ends.
The shell supports useful degraded/offline states without treating cached visibility as continuing authority.
Public and pre-authentication routes use a separate minimal shell without private taxonomy, counts, names, recents, or tenant structure.
Semantic or AI retrieval is separately gated and default OFF in the initial core shell.
The Founder-approved visual-system V0.3.1 remains immutable and incorporated by exact bytes and SHA-256, never silently rewritten.

Display authorized commands, confirm or step up where required, execute idempotently, and preserve outcome evidence.

requirements.statement: Resolve authenticated identity, session validity, current memberships, candidate contexts, permission projection, configuration version, and shell version before protected content renders.
requirements.prohibited: Protected content, route names, counts, or tenant structure appearing before authorization completes.
requirements.failure: Render a neutral protected-loading state, then route to sign-in, context selection, denied, or safe recovery.

requirements.statement: Keep the selected tenant, organization, and facility visibly identified on every private shell surface.
requirements.prohibited: Silent context changes or an unlabeled active context.
requirements.failure: Freeze risky actions, show context uncertainty, and require explicit selection.

requirements.statement: Require explicit confirmation before a user changes to a materially different tenant or facility context.
requirements.prohibited: Inferring context from the last clicked record, search result, or stale cache.
requirements.failure: Cancel the switch and preserve the current known context.

requirements.statement: On context switch, re-evaluate permissions and invalidate routes, search, recents, pins, badges, drafts, and caches that do not belong to the new context.
requirements.prohibited: Carrying protected state across contexts.
requirements.failure: Clear incompatible state, refresh projections, and record the failed or completed switch.

requirements.statement: Use persona defaults only to select ordering, emphasis, and initial landing after authorization filtering.
requirements.prohibited: Treating a persona label as a permission or source of truth.
requirements.failure: Use a neutral authorized landing and log configuration drift.

requirements.statement: When a user has multiple valid contexts and no safe default, require context selection before private domain content appears.
requirements.prohibited: Selecting a context using guesswork or a hidden ranking.
requirements.failure: Show a disclosure-minimized context picker.

requirements.statement: Separate public, invitation, recovery, and authentication surfaces from the private application shell.
requirements.prohibited: Leaking private taxonomy, names, counts, or recent activity on pre-authentication surfaces.
requirements.failure: Render the minimal pre-authentication shell only.

requirements.statement: Preserve one stable correlation identifier across shell bootstrap, context selection, route resolution, and downstream diagnostic events without storing secrets.
requirements.prohibited: Logging tokens, credentials, private message bodies, or unrestricted search text.
requirements.failure: Redact the payload and retain only privacy-minimized diagnostics.

requirements.statement: Maintain a versioned route registry with stable route ID, owner, path pattern, capability, sensitivity, context requirements, lifecycle status, and deep-link policy.
requirements.prohibited: Unregistered routes or duplicate route ownership.
requirements.failure: Block publication and open a configuration finding.

requirements.statement: Build visible navigation from current route eligibility and permission projection rather than a static role-name menu.
requirements.prohibited: Showing a menu item as proof that access is granted.
requirements.failure: Hide or disable the item and reauthorize at destination.

requirements.statement: Reauthorize every route load, refresh, Back/Forward navigation, bookmark, and deep-link open.
requirements.prohibited: Relying solely on prior menu visibility or client-side route guards.
requirements.failure: Return a disclosure-safe denied or reauthentication state.

requirements.statement: Use a persistent or collapsible rail on suitable desktop and tablet widths, with keyboard-operable groups and deterministic collapse behavior.
requirements.prohibited: Hover-only access, unreachable collapsed controls, or loss of current-location indication.
requirements.failure: Expand to an accessible fallback and preserve content access.

requirements.statement: Use a bounded mobile bottom navigation for highest-frequency authorized destinations and an accessible More destination for the remainder.
requirements.prohibited: Overcrowded, horizontally scrolling, or permission-leaking mobile navigation.
requirements.failure: Reduce to the approved bounded set and expose the remainder through More.

requirements.statement: Keep the current destination, parent group, active context, and unsaved-work state perceivable without relying on color alone.
requirements.prohibited: Ambiguous location or color-only active indicators.
requirements.failure: Add text, icon, state, and assistive labels.

requirements.statement: Generate breadcrumbs from registered route relationships and domain-owned labels, not from raw URLs.
requirements.prohibited: Exposing identifiers, inaccessible ancestors, or stale names in breadcrumbs.
requirements.failure: Suppress unavailable ancestors and retain a safe current-location label.

requirements.statement: Provide predictable Back behavior that respects browser history, modal origin, and context boundaries.
requirements.prohibited: A Back action that silently changes tenant context or loses unsaved work.
requirements.failure: Warn, preserve the draft where authorized, or route to a safe parent.

requirements.statement: Treat deep-link descriptors as non-authoritative pointers that may carry only bounded target and context hints.
requirements.prohibited: Embedding permission, secrets, protected names, or permanent authority in a link.
requirements.failure: Reject or neutralize the link and require fresh authorization.

requirements.statement: Use distinct not-found, denied, unavailable, and failed states internally while minimizing disclosure externally.
requirements.prohibited: Confirming the existence of a protected resource through error wording or timing.
requirements.failure: Return the appropriate safe state with a permitted recovery action.

requirements.statement: Store shell preferences as private actor-scoped configuration and never as a source of access.
requirements.prohibited: Shared preferences that expose another user’s activity or override policy.
requirements.failure: Reset to approved defaults and record a privacy finding.

requirements.statement: Reauthorize recents, pins, favorites, and saved views every time they are read or opened.
requirements.prohibited: Continuing visibility after relationship, role, context, or permission loss.
requirements.failure: Suppress the item and invalidate its display metadata.

requirements.statement: Store saved views as filter, sort, column, and presentation definitions without storing protected result rows.
requirements.prohibited: Persisting a private dataset inside a view configuration.
requirements.failure: Strip result data and require regeneration under current authority.

requirements.statement: Allow tenant administrators to configure only an approved allowlist of labels, ordering, group visibility, and defaults.
requirements.prohibited: Renaming authoritative domain concepts, hiding mandatory safety routes, or granting access through configuration.
requirements.failure: Reject the configuration and keep the last valid version.

requirements.statement: Provide a reset-to-default action for user shell preferences without deleting domain records.
requirements.prohibited: A preference reset that alters tasks, horse records, billing, or communication state.
requirements.failure: Abort and isolate the preference operation.

requirements.statement: Expire or trim private recents according to classification, age, and user controls.
requirements.prohibited: Indefinite retention of sensitive browsing history by default.
requirements.failure: Remove expired pointers and preserve only required audit evidence.

requirements.statement: Keep badge counts and summaries minimum-necessary and independently revalidated.
requirements.prohibited: Showing protected names, health details, financial amounts, safeguarding facts, or stale counts in the shell.
requirements.failure: Replace with a generic authorized indicator or suppress the badge.

requirements.statement: Do not use behavioral advertising, unrelated profiling, or manipulative engagement ranking in shell personalization.
requirements.prohibited: Cross-context tracking, dark patterns, or personalization aimed at minors.
requirements.failure: Disable the feature, preserve evidence, and open a governance finding.

requirements.statement: Treat search as an authorized view of existing source truth and never as a source of ownership, custody, consent, relationship, professional authority, financial responsibility, or permission.
requirements.prohibited: Creating authority or factual truth from a result, rank, suggestion, or index entry.
requirements.failure: Display source context and require the authoritative workflow for consequential action.

requirements.statement: Scope global search to the current actor and active context unless a separately approved discovery mode explicitly narrows and explains another scope.
requirements.prohibited: Identifiable cross-tenant search by default.
requirements.failure: Return no cross-tenant result and record prohibited enumeration attempts.

requirements.statement: Apply permission and classification filtering before retrieval where technically possible and again before presentation and open.
requirements.prohibited: Relying on post-render masking or client-only filtering.
requirements.failure: Suppress the result and invalidate the affected index projection.

requirements.statement: Exclude safeguarding records, precise location, private communications, credentials, secrets, raw financial identifiers, and other protected fields from general search.
requirements.prohibited: Indexing protected content into ordinary global search.
requirements.failure: Remove the fields, reindex, assess exposure, and preserve incident evidence.

requirements.statement: Apply heightened protections to minors, guardianship, location, contact, and recommendation results.
requirements.prohibited: Open-ended minor directories, contact discovery, or behavioral recommendation.
requirements.failure: Suppress, narrow, and route to a specialized authorized workflow.

requirements.statement: Keep autocomplete and suggestions permission-bound, minimum-necessary, context-aware, and resistant to enumeration.
requirements.prohibited: Revealing inaccessible names or record existence through prefix probing.
requirements.failure: Rate-limit, suppress, and emit an abuse signal.

requirements.statement: Label result type, authoritative source, current context, freshness, and meaningful limitation where needed for safe interpretation.
requirements.prohibited: Presenting stale or derived data as current authoritative truth.
requirements.failure: Mark stale, restrict action, or route to refresh.

requirements.statement: Use neutral, explainable ranking based on relevance, recency, domain priority, and user-selected filters.
requirements.prohibited: Paid placement, secret favoritism, or ranking that changes authority.
requirements.failure: Fall back to deterministic neutral ordering and record the configuration defect.

requirements.statement: Propagate correction, revocation, restriction, deletion, and relationship changes into indexes, suggestions, caches, and result snippets within defined service bounds.
requirements.prohibited: Continuing to surface withdrawn or unauthorized information.
requirements.failure: Suppress immediately where possible, queue repair, and expose freshness status.

requirements.statement: Minimize ordinary query history and provide proportionate user controls; apply heightened logging only to defined high-risk or privileged searches.
requirements.prohibited: Indefinite full-text query retention or hidden privileged browsing.
requirements.failure: Redact, shorten retention, and require privileged-search review.

requirements.statement: Detect and respond to scraping, harvesting, stalking, enumeration, bulk export patterns, and location probing.
requirements.prohibited: Unbounded automated discovery or silent bulk extraction.
requirements.failure: Throttle, block, challenge, alert, and preserve privacy-minimized evidence.

requirements.statement: Keep semantic or AI-assisted retrieval default OFF until separately authorized with source attribution, tenant isolation, permission filtering, evaluation, disablement, and provider controls.
requirements.prohibited: Connecting customer data to an unapproved model or shared training corpus.
requirements.failure: Disable the feature and remove generated or indexed derivatives.

requirements.statement: Register every command with stable ID, owner, display rule, input schema, execution endpoint, risk level, authorization rule, and evidence rule.
requirements.prohibited: Free-form executable commands or commands without a domain owner.
requirements.failure: Do not publish the command.

requirements.statement: Separate command discovery authorization from execution-time authorization and re-evaluate immediately before execution.
requirements.prohibited: Executing because the command was visible earlier.
requirements.failure: Deny, explain safely, and refresh the command list.

requirements.statement: Require confirmation, recent authentication, step-up, or dual control for commands classified as consequential.
requirements.prohibited: One-click execution of high-risk financial, safeguarding, access, or deletion actions.
requirements.failure: Hold the request pending the required control.

requirements.statement: Use idempotency keys and explicit pending, completed, failed, canceled, and reconciled states for effectful quick actions.
requirements.prohibited: Duplicate effects caused by retry, refresh, or double activation.
requirements.failure: Return the prior result or place the action into reconciliation.

requirements.statement: Limit Quick Create to registered domain-owned forms and current create authority in the active context.
requirements.prohibited: A generic shell form that invents domain rules or creates in the wrong tenant.
requirements.failure: Block launch and direct to context correction.

requirements.statement: Preserve unsaved quick-action input only within authorized context and classification limits.
requirements.prohibited: Carrying a protected draft across users, contexts, or expired sessions.
requirements.failure: Clear or securely quarantine the draft.

requirements.statement: Keep shell commands keyboard accessible, searchable without disclosure, and operable without pointer-only interaction.
requirements.prohibited: Mouse-only, hover-only, or unannounced command behavior.
requirements.failure: Expose an accessible alternative and suppress unsupported shortcuts.

requirements.statement: Never let a shell command bypass the domain workflow, validation, audit, consent, or approval requirements owned by another PIA.
requirements.prohibited: Treating shell convenience as substantive authority.
requirements.failure: Route to the domain-owned workflow and preserve the attempted shortcut evidence.

requirements.statement: Provide deterministic loading, ready, empty, denied, unavailable, degraded, stale, conflict, and error states for every shell surface.
requirements.prohibited: Blank screens, misleading success, or one generic state for materially different conditions.
requirements.failure: Render the safe state and a permitted recovery path.

requirements.statement: Prevent protected-content flash during bootstrap, context change, session expiry, route transition, and cache restore.
requirements.prohibited: Showing prior authorized content before current authorization resolves.
requirements.failure: Mask protected regions until resolution.

requirements.statement: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA for web and equivalent native-platform accessibility expectations, including keyboard, focus, names, roles, reflow, zoom, text scaling, and reduced motion.
requirements.prohibited: Color-only meaning, hidden focus, inaccessible modal traps, or essential image-only text.
requirements.failure: Block release or disable the affected presentation.

requirements.statement: Use at least 44 by 44 CSS pixel or point targets for primary field actions unless an equivalent accessible pattern is documented and tested.
requirements.prohibited: Tiny high-frequency controls unsuitable for barn conditions.
requirements.failure: Use a larger control or alternate action surface.

requirements.statement: Preserve critical actions in glare, gloves, one-handed use, intermittent connectivity, and small-screen conditions.
requirements.prohibited: Precision-only gestures or low-contrast operational controls.
requirements.failure: Expose a simplified text-first fallback.

requirements.statement: Keep serious workflows free from celebratory animation, playful copy, mascot treatment, or decorative typography that could trivialize risk.
requirements.prohibited: Stead or decorative celebration during injury, medication, safeguarding, payment approval, security, legal, or outage workflows.
requirements.failure: Suppress decoration and render a neutral serious-workflow state.

requirements.statement: Incorporate the approved visual-system V0.3.1 by exact source bytes and SHA-256 without editing its approved content.
requirements.prohibited: Recreating, rewriting, or silently superseding the approved component inside this candidate.
requirements.failure: Stop package assembly and obtain the verified exact source file.

requirements.statement: Apply the approved visual hierarchy, typography roles, color separation, icon system, and Stead restrictions only within the scope and conditions recorded by V0.3.1.
requirements.prohibited: Extending visual approval into product behavior or activating Stead without separate authority.
requirements.failure: Use neutral shell defaults and open a design deviation.

requirements.statement: Cache only explicitly approved shell metadata and authorized minimum-necessary pointers with tenant, actor, version, expiry, classification, and revocation watermark.
requirements.prohibited: Caching unrestricted search results, protected snippets, secrets, or cross-tenant state.
requirements.failure: Purge the cache and assess exposure.

requirements.statement: Display persistent offline, stale, queued, failed, and synchronization-conflict status without implying server confirmation.
requirements.prohibited: Silent local success or hiding stale authority.
requirements.failure: Keep the action pending or blocked and explain next safe step.

requirements.statement: Do not treat cached route visibility, prior search results, badges, or context as continuing authority.
requirements.prohibited: Opening protected content solely because it was previously cached.
requirements.failure: Restrict to approved offline projection or require reconnection.

requirements.statement: On reconnect, refresh identity, session, context, permissions, route registry, configuration, revocation watermark, and affected cached pointers before privileged actions.
requirements.prohibited: Replaying stale actions before authority refresh.
requirements.failure: Hold the queue and reconcile each action.

requirements.statement: Bind queued shell actions to actor, device, tenant, facility, command version, idempotency key, and creation time.
requirements.prohibited: Replaying an action in a different context or under a different user.
requirements.failure: Reject and preserve a reconciliation record.

requirements.statement: Support secure device sign-out, session revocation, and cache purge with a documented limitation when the device remains unreachable.
requirements.prohibited: Claiming immediate remote deletion when it cannot be proven.
requirements.failure: Revoke server authority, mark purge pending, and communicate the limitation.

requirements.statement: Use least privilege and field-level projection for shell bootstrap, navigation, search, badges, recents, support, and diagnostics.
requirements.prohibited: A broad administrator label granting universal shell visibility.
requirements.failure: Deny the projection and require action-specific authority.

requirements.statement: Require support mode to be separately authorized, purpose-bound, time-limited, visibly indicated, attributable, and fully auditable.
requirements.prohibited: Hidden impersonation, unrestricted browsing, or support access without a valid target and purpose.
requirements.failure: Block or terminate the support session and alert.

requirements.statement: Minimize telemetry and diagnostics and prohibit secrets, credentials, unrestricted queries, message bodies, sensitive health detail, and safeguarding content in ordinary logs.
requirements.prohibited: Using observability as a shadow data store.
requirements.failure: Redact, rotate, investigate, and correct instrumentation.

requirements.statement: Apply safeguarding restrictions across route visibility, search, suggestions, notifications, badges, recents, exports, support, and caches.
requirements.prohibited: A general shell feature bypassing a protective restriction.
requirements.failure: Suppress access, invalidate derived state, and escalate under the safeguarding process.

requirements.statement: Expose a versioned shell-bootstrap contract with explicit context candidates, authorized capabilities, route version, configuration version, freshness, and safe failure codes.
requirements.prohibited: Returning full domain datasets or ambiguous authorization state in bootstrap.
requirements.failure: Return a minimal safe response and require recovery.

requirements.statement: Use versioned search, command, preference, recents, notification-summary, support-session, and configuration contracts with schema validation and backwards-compatibility rules.
requirements.prohibited: Ad hoc unversioned payloads or silent field reinterpretation.
requirements.failure: Reject incompatible requests and retain the prior supported contract.

requirements.statement: Publish attributable events for context changes, privileged searches, consequential commands, support sessions, configuration publication, and route lifecycle changes.
requirements.prohibited: Relying solely on client analytics for consequential evidence.
requirements.failure: Fail closed where evidence is mandatory or queue an auditable event.

requirements.statement: Run index repair, revocation propagation, cache expiry, badge refresh, saved-view cleanup, and configuration validation as bounded idempotent jobs with observable outcomes.
requirements.prohibited: Unbounded jobs, duplicate effects, or silent partial completion.
requirements.failure: Pause, retry safely, reconcile, and alert.

requirements.statement: Scope feature flags by environment, tenant, cohort, capability, and version with safe defaults, named owner, expiry, and emergency disablement.
requirements.prohibited: A flag that grants authority, stores secrets, or remains indefinitely without owner.
requirements.failure: Use the safe default and block publication.

requirements.statement: Keep secrets, signing keys, provider credentials, and private tokens outside source, client bundles, PIA artifacts, screenshots, logs, and configuration payloads.
requirements.prohibited: Embedding or documenting live secrets in the shell package.
requirements.failure: Revoke, rotate, redact, and treat as a security incident.

requirements.statement: Inventory current routes, menus, labels, deep links, role-based shortcuts, search fields, caches, preferences, and legacy shell assets before migration.
requirements.prohibited: Replacing the shell without a reconciliation map or historical evidence.
requirements.failure: Stop migration and complete the inventory.

requirements.statement: Roll out shell changes through controlled environments and cohorts with preflight validation, telemetry, stop conditions, rollback, and post-release verification.
requirements.prohibited: All-at-once activation without tested rollback.
requirements.failure: Stop rollout and restore the last verified configuration or build.

requirements.statement: Decommission routes, commands, search fields, and assets by removing active exposure, migrating lawful preferences/links, invalidating caches, and preserving history.
requirements.prohibited: Deleting history or leaving a retired entry point active.
requirements.failure: Quarantine the route and complete decommission evidence.

requirements.statement: Provide operational dashboards for bootstrap failures, route denials, context-switch defects, search latency/errors, stale indexes, abuse signals, support sessions, job failures, and configuration drift.
requirements.prohibited: Metrics that expose protected content or falsely imply operational readiness.
requirements.failure: Use privacy-minimized aggregates and mark evidence state accurately.

requirements.statement: Provide bounded administrative tools for route/configuration validation, cache invalidation, index repair, support-session termination, and feature disablement.
requirements.prohibited: Direct database editing or unrestricted production browsing as the standard support path.
requirements.failure: Disable the unsafe tool and use a controlled procedure.

requirements.statement: Reconcile the as-built shell to every applicable requirement, source, decision, route, contract, test, evidence item, and incorporated visual-system hash before verification.
requirements.prohibited: Claiming conformance from screenshots, demos, or unexecuted tests.
requirements.failure: Classify drift and block verification until resolved or formally accepted.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall resolve authenticated identity, session validity, current memberships, candidate contexts, permission projection, configuration version, and shell version before protected content renders.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Protected content, route names, counts, or tenant structure appearing before authorization completes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall keep the selected tenant, organization, and facility visibly identified on every private shell surface.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Silent context changes or an unlabeled active context.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall require explicit confirmation before a user changes to a materially different tenant or facility context.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Inferring context from the last clicked record, search result, or stale cache.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall on context switch, re-evaluate permissions and invalidate routes, search, recents, pins, badges, drafts, and caches that do not belong to the new context.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Carrying protected state across contexts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall use persona defaults only to select ordering, emphasis, and initial landing after authorization filtering.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Treating a persona label as a permission or source of truth.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall when a user has multiple valid contexts and no safe default, require context selection before private domain content appears.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Selecting a context using guesswork or a hidden ranking.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall separate public, invitation, recovery, and authentication surfaces from the private application shell.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Leaking private taxonomy, names, counts, or recent activity on pre-authentication surfaces.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall preserve one stable correlation identifier across shell bootstrap, context selection, route resolution, and downstream diagnostic events without storing secrets.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Logging tokens, credentials, private message bodies, or unrestricted search text.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a current actor, session, context, configuration, and source state, when the covered shell behavior occurs, then the system shall maintain a versioned route registry with stable route ID, owner, path pattern, capability, sensitivity, context requirements, lifecycle status, and deep-link policy.
acceptance_criteria.prohibited_result: Unregistered routes or duplicate route ownership.

readiness.question: Can engineering build the capability without making unauthorized product decisions?
readiness.basis: The candidate defines scope, 76 requirements, 20 workflows, 22 entities, route/search/command/offline contracts, permissions, work packages, acceptance, tests, and failure behavior. Candidate Founder decisions and source freeze remain prerequisites to implementation authorization.
readiness.gate_effect: Documentary buildability is positive; implementation remains unauthorized.

readiness.question: Can quality assurance determine objectively whether the capability works?
readiness.basis: Each requirement maps to an objective acceptance criterion, positive/negative design test, evidence item, workflow, entity, and work package; 12 golden paths and 30 adversarial scenarios are defined. No test has been executed.
readiness.gate_effect: QA can construct executable verification; verification is unperformed.

readiness.question: Can a reviewer trace the capability to EquineSync’s controlling governance and the MIAP?
readiness.basis: The locked baseline, Master Standard hashes, approved visual component hash, source families, requirements, and lifecycle gates are linked. Exact current path, version, status, checksum, and supersession accession remain open for several sources, and the repository snapshot is not frozen.
readiness.gate_effect: Fresh structured review and source accession are required before implementation authorization.

readiness.question: Can EquineSync safely operate, support, monitor, recover, and maintain the capability?
readiness.basis: Operational requirements and evidence categories are designed, but no authorized implementation, assigned operational owners, active monitoring, support tooling, backup/restore, incident exercise, or rollback rehearsal exists.

readiness.question: Can the Founder determine whether the capability is ready for first-user enrollment?
readiness.basis: The complete shell is not Founder-approved, implemented, verified, operationally proven, or enrollment-authorized. Open P1 documentary and lifecycle conditions remain.
